author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
method: Look for a discrete holomorphic observable on the square lattice analogous to Smirnov's on the triangular lattice.
obstruction: Only the weak (contour) half of discrete holomorphicity holds for the q=1 parafermion on the square lattice.
result: Smirnov's argument needs the three-arm colour-switching symmetry, which on the triangular lattice comes from site self-duality; on Z^2 bond percolation the dual is the shifted square lattice and the exploration interface lives on the medial lattice, where the parafermionic observable F(z) = E[e^{i sigma W(z)} 1_{z on interface}] with spin sigma = ... satisfies only half of the discrete Cauchy-Riemann relations (the contour-integral relations, as for FK models with q not 2). A concrete check: for the q=1 FK model the parafermionic observable has spin sigma = 1/3 and the relation sum over edges around a face vanishes, which gives crossing exponent bounds but not holomorphicity; the missing half is what conformal invariance needs. No new observable found.
correction_note: DRAFT source correction by w417, 2026-10-10; independent review pending. In the convention F(e)=E[exp(i sigma W(e,e_b)) 1_{e in gamma}], Duminil-Copin, Divergence of the correlation length for critical planar FK percolation, Conjecture 1 Eq.(3.3), PDF page index 9, gives sigma=1-(2/pi)arccos(sqrt(q)/2). Thus q=1 has sigma=1/3, while sigma=2/3 has q=3. https://www.ihes.fr/~duminil/publi/divergenceFK.pdf . The historical failed-route assessment is retained; this correction does not prove conformal invariance.
